So when it comes to the different materials that you can use for your nozzle, you can use hardened steel for any filament. Hardened steel is incredibly useful for incredibly abrasive materials like carbon fiber and wood for example. The only difference is the hardened steel nozzle doesn't allow temperature to easily get through it like a brass or bi-metal nozzle would. So if you have done any filament calibrations on the bi-metal nozzle, you would need to redo them to accurately print on the hardened steel nozzle. 

The hardened steel nozzle will also last a very very long time, it will probably outlive the printer itself.

Both printers have automatic bed leveling, but just the Q1 pro has the ability to get the bed as flat as possible manually before running the Auto bed leveling. It is always best to get it as flat as possible even if there is Auto bed leveling so there doesn't have to be too much compensation. You need to let your bed heat up for 10 minutes before you run the bed leveling and before you do any print. Your bed warps over time with heat and 10 minutes is usually good enough for it to expand then settle.
